smell: The 'step' attr key carries TWO distinct value types across sites in the same file: step.ID() (machine slug, e.g. 'destroy-infrastructure') at lines 132/149/162/164/177, and step.Name() (human label, e.g. 'destroy infrastructure') at lines 90/142. A JSON pipeline grouping by step cannot tell them apart and fanning out fails: the 'started' record carries id, the matching 'skipped' record carries the name.
evidence:
L90:  o.logger.Info("step: skipped", "step", step.Name(), "reason", result.SkipReason)
L142: o.logger.Info("step: skipped (already done)", "step", step.Name())
L149: o.logger.Info("step: started", "step", step.ID(), "name", step.Name())
L162: o.logger.Error("step: failed", "step", step.ID(), ..., "err", err)
severity_reason: un-idiomatic pattern that the repo will trip on the first time someone tries to correlate step-level slog records — same key, two value types breaks every downstream consumer. Rubric §4/un-idiomatic-pattern.
fix_summary: Standardise on step.ID() under the 'step' key everywhere in this file; pass step.Name() under 'name' (already used at line 149) for human display. Lines 90 and 142 swap step.Name() to step.ID() and add 'name', step.Name() if the human label is still wanted.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets — Prefer structured attrs (logger.Warn(..., err, err))
Google SRE — Structured Logging — stable field schema

smell: Pervasive `tui.Info(fmt.Sprintf(...))` / `p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf(...))` pattern across ~50 sites in cli/ and distribution/okd/. Stringifying interpolated values into the message text bypasses RedactHandler structured-attr scrub (which only rewrites attr keys/values), kills slog-handler ability to filter by field, and prevents downstream JSON pipelines from extracting the dynamic value (path, cluster name, count, duration). CLAUDE.md is explicit: prefer structured attrs over fmt.Sprintf so the handler can inspect values.
evidence:
helpers.go:32: tui.Error(fmt.Sprintf("configuration file not found: %s", configFile))
helpers.go:296: tui.Info(fmt.Sprintf("deployment complete (total time: %s)", duration))
deploy.go:255: tui.Info(fmt.Sprintf("configuration saved to %s", path))
destroy.go:104: tui.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("this will destroy cluster '%s'...", cfg.Cluster.Name))
setup/phase.go:136: p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("setup: cluster config saved to %s", clusterDir))
severity_reason: un-idiomatic pattern that has bitten the repo before; CLAUDE.md explicitly bans this exact shape because the redaction handler cannot sweep values that are already string-melted into the message. Rubric §4/un-idiomatic-pattern.
fix_summary: Mechanical sweep: every `tui.X(fmt.Sprintf("prefix: %s", v))` becomes `tui.X("prefix", tui.LF("key", v))`; every `p.Log.X(fmt.Sprintf("prefix: %s", v))` becomes `p.Log.X("prefix", "key", v)`. ~50 sites; one PR per package keeps churn reviewable. Roll-up message stays static; values move to attrs.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/cli/root.go:L121 — tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))

smell: firewall.Configure / firewall.RemoveRules / openPort take a *slog.Logger but never normalise nil through logutil.OrNop. DetectBackend (L80) explicitly tolerates nil; the rest of the package does not. Today every caller passes non-nil p.Log so the latent panic is unreachable — but the *slog.Logger nil-tolerance contract diverges within the file (DetectBackend says nil-tolerant, everyone else assumes non-nil), inviting a future caller to honour the documented nil-tolerance and crash.
evidence:
L80: // DetectBackend ... logger may be nil; when nil, no probe-failure observability is emitted.
L117: func Configure(ctx context.Context, ports []Port, permanent bool, logger *slog.Logger) error {
L121:     logger.Warn("no active firewall detected, skipping firewall configuration")  // panics if nil
L125:     logger.Info(fmt.Sprintf("firewall: configuring using %s", backend))
severity_reason: latent panic; not reachable today (all 4 callers pass p.Log) but the documented nil-tolerance asymmetry within the package is the kind of footgun that lands as a postmortem six months later.
fix_summary: At the top of Configure, RemoveRules, openPort, modifyPort: `logger = logutil.OrNop(logger)`. Or remove the 'logger may be nil' clause from DetectBackend doc and require non-nil everywhere. Pick one nil-policy and apply it package-wide.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — internal/logutil.NopLogger is the canonical no-op logger
repo-counter-example: internal/addon/manager.go:L53-L55 — NewManager normalises nil to NopLogger

smell: Manager.InstallAll failure-log at line 98 drops the `addon` attr that every neighbouring site emits (L90, L101, L103, L120, L128, L184, L186). When two addons fail in the same run, the resulting log records are indistinguishable — no way to grep `addon=flux` to see all events for one addon.
severity_reason: observability gap — failure-log loses the correlation key (addon name) that the rest of the file consistently carries. Trivial fix; affects post-mortem readability of multi-addon failures.
fix_summary: Add `"addon", info.DisplayName` to the L98 attr list, matching the shape of L101 and L103 in the same loop.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/addon/manager.go:L101-L103 — surrounding sites carry the addon attr

smell: services.Dnsmasq logs `cleanup: refusing critical path` three times in close succession (L155, L167, L176) without including which path was refused. The error message inside guardErr names the path, but a structured attr is missing — operators reading text logs see three identical lines with different `err` values; JSON pipelines cannot group by 'which file was rejected'.
evidence:
L155: logger.Warn("cleanup: refusing critical path", "err", guardErr)
L167: logger.Warn("cleanup: refusing critical path", "err", guardErr)
L176: logger.Warn("cleanup: refusing critical path", "err", guardErr)
severity_reason: observability gap — destroy-path logs missing the 'what got refused' field weakens the audit trail on a destructive operation. Mild because guardErr.Error() does carry the path; this is field-discipline polish.
fix_summary: Add `"path", configPath` (or `"path", cfg`, `"path", backup`) at each of the three sites so the path is queryable separately from the error chain.

smell: Acceptable per-attempt logging in the CSR-approval poll loop already de-duplicates identical consecutive errors via lastCSRWarnMsg (L122-L161): first occurrence at Warn, repeats demoted to Debug. This is the canonical correct shape for a poll/retry loop. Flagged here as a positive counter-example so the audit does not accidentally regress this on a later sweep — fix is to document the idiom, not to change the code.
fix_summary: Document this de-duplication idiom (msg == lastWarnMsg means Debug, else Warn) in CLAUDE.md §concurrency or §logging-conventions as the repo canonical poll-loop log-once pattern. Reference from any future poll-loop site review.

smell: runCheck calls package-level slog.Debug (L72, L77) which routes through slog.Default(), implicitly coupled to cli.Execute setting `slog.SetDefault(tui.SimpleLogger())`. If a future caller embeds version.BackgroundCheck without going through cli.Execute (e.g. an alternate cmd/ entry point or an in-process test that does not set the default), these records bypass the redaction handler and emit through stdlib text handler — which lacks the RedactHandler middleware. The internal/runlock/runlock.go:L69 site has the same shape.
evidence:
updatecheck.go:72: slog.Debug("update check fetch failed", "err", err)
updatecheck.go:77: slog.Debug("update check cache save failed", "err", err)
runlock.go:69:    slog.Warn("runlock: os.Hostname failed, using unknown", "err", hostErr)
severity_reason: latent observability gap — works in current call graph because cli.Execute always runs first, but binds two leaf packages to the cli setup ordering. Fix is mechanical and removes coupling.
fix_summary: Either (a) thread a *slog.Logger through BackgroundCheck/Acquire so the caller controls the sink (matches every other domain package — orchestrator, addon, terraform), or (b) accept the implicit coupling and add a one-line doc comment on each package-level slog call: 'depends on cli.Execute setting slog.Default; safe in the okdctl process'. Option (a) is symmetric with the rest of the codebase.

smell: `tui.Warn("skipping HostNetwork conversion: " + err.Error())` concatenates the err string into the message text (string-melt), bypassing RedactHandler structured-attr scrub. The error-stringification pattern (CLAUDE.md flags `slog.String("error", err.Error())` as 'kills structured handling'); the same anti-pattern in concat form.
severity_reason: err-stringified pattern; in this site the error does not appear to carry credentials, but the shape is the one CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids and reviewers will keep flagging it.
fix_summary: Replace with `tui.Warn("skipping HostNetwork conversion", tui.LF("err", err))`.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/cli/root.go:L121 — tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))

smell: execute() pins run_id via tui.SetRunID for every subsequent slog record (good — set later in phase entry points), but the cobra command tree itself (rootCmd.ExecuteContext at L113) does NOT log a 'started okdctl <verb>' / 'finished okdctl <verb> in <duration>' span pair around its execution. No top-level span boundary in stderr text logs; a JSON pipeline parsing mid-run records cannot tell which invocation a record belongs to until SetRunID lands. Preflight records, configureLogging errors emit before run_id is set.
evidence:
L77: slog.SetDefault(tui.SimpleLogger())
L113: err := rootCmd.ExecuteContext(ctx)
L121: tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))
# no Info("okdctl: started", ...) or matching finished record at this layer
severity_reason: observability polish — correlation works once SetRunID fires inside subcommand RunE, but pre-RunID records (preflight failures from cmd/okdctl/main.go, configureLogging errors) are orphaned. Affects cross-run debugging only.
fix_summary: Generate run_id at the top of execute() (before BackgroundCheck), call tui.SetRunID(id) immediately, then emit a single `tui.Info("okdctl: started", tui.LF("argv", strings.Join(os.Args[1:], " ")))` and a matching `tui.Info("okdctl: finished", tui.LF("duration", elapsed), tui.LF("exit_code", code))` in the deferred-exit path. Pulls run_id earlier in the lifecycle so preflight records carry it too (requires moving cmd/okdctl/main.go preflight after run_id init).
rule_source: Google SRE — Structured Logging — span boundaries

smell: installSystemPackages emits Debug per package via `p.Log.Debug(fmt.Sprintf("packages: %s not found", pkg))` and likewise for 'already installed'. Same fmt.Sprintf-into-message anti-pattern as obs:6424733c, but this one is in a tight per-element loop that runs at deploy time. Same fix pattern; called out separately because Debug-level traffic is the primary signal new operators turn on with --verbose, and structured attrs make `--log-format=json | jq` immediately useful.
evidence:
L312: p.Log.Debug(fmt.Sprintf("packages: %s not found", pkg))
L314: p.Log.Debug(fmt.Sprintf("packages: %s already installed", pkg))
L323: p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("packages: installing %d missing package(s)", len(toInstall)))
severity_reason: covered by the umbrella obs:6424733c finding; flagged here because Debug-traffic structuredness is high-leverage for --verbose users, and this is one of the densest call sites.
fix_summary: L312: `p.Log.Debug("packages: not found", "pkg", pkg)`. L314: `p.Log.Debug("packages: already installed", "pkg", pkg)`. L323: `p.Log.Info("packages: installing missing", "count", len(toInstall))`. Caller can then `jq 'select(.pkg=="haproxy")'` cleanly.

smell: `p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("workers: starting %d worker nodes", cfg.Topology.Workers.Count))` — count goes into the message, not as an attr. Specific instance of obs:6424733c worth flagging because it is the only 'span: started' marker for the workers step and wants `count` as a queryable attr (alert thresholds, dashboards).
evidence: L20: p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("workers: starting %d worker nodes", cfg.Topology.Workers.Count))
severity_reason: covered by obs:6424733c umbrella; called out specifically because as a span-start record, the count is high-value as an attr.

smell: verify.go iterates degraded operators and emits one Warn per operator (L132-134), then immediately a summary Warn with the count (L136-137). On a 30-operator cluster this is 31 Warn lines for the same event. The aggregated form would be one Warn carrying the slice of degraded names — sufficient signal for an alert pipeline, easier to read in a TTY.
severity_reason: chatty log pattern; not a blocker because operator counts are bounded (~30) but the 'one warn per element + one summary' shape is exactly what 'log-once-per-event' targets.
fix_summary: Drop the per-operator loop; emit one structured warn carrying the list: `p.Log.Warn("cluster: operators degraded", "count", len(degraded), "names", degraded)`. Loses one fewer log line per operator and gains a queryable list attr.

smell: redactAny only catches *url.URL/url.URL with userinfo and types implementing Redacted(); does NOT catch raw structs whose fields are credential-bearing (e.g. `slog.Any("creds", credentials.ProxmoxCredentials{Password: pwd})`). The CLAUDE.md guarantee — slog records pass through internal/logutil.RedactHandler ... attrs whose keys contain password/token/secret/api_key are rewritten to [redacted] — applies only when the credential is the direct value of a secret-keyed attr, not when it is a field inside a struct passed under a benign key like 'creds' or 'config'.
severity_reason: redaction-sink coverage gap; the only mitigation today is that credentials.ProxmoxCredentials should implement Redacted() any. If it does not (or any future cred-bearing struct does not), `slog.Any("x", creds)` leaks the password verbatim through the JSON formatter. Rubric §4/credential-exposure (latent).
fix_summary: Two complementary defences: (1) verify credentials.ProxmoxCredentials implements Redacted() any (audit-errors should already cover this); (2) add a type-switch case for known credential types in redactAny (`case *credentials.ProxmoxCredentials:` returning a redacted clone) as defence-in-depth — caller mistakes do not leak. Document the contract: 'credential types must implement Redacted()' in logutil/redact.go package doc.

smell: configureLogging defaults `--log-format=text` regardless of TTY state. When stderr is piped (e.g. `okdctl deploy 2>&1 | tee log.txt`), text-formatted ANSI/colored output bleeds into the captured file unless the user explicitly passes `--log-format=json`. The repo correctly disables progress bars when stderr is non-TTY (L59-64), but the equivalent format auto-switch (text-when-TTY, json-when-pipe) is missing — this is the textbook 'handler-no-tty-switch' pattern. Note: progressBars already keys off stderrIsTTY; adding a parallel default-format switch is symmetric.
evidence:
L51: effectiveLevel := logLevel
L52: switch { case logQuiet: effectiveLevel = "error"; case logVerbose: effectiveLevel = "debug" }
L59: stderrIsTTY := term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stderr.Fd()))
# logFormat is read straight from the flag — never tty-modulated
L66: return tui.ConfigureLoggers(effectiveLevel, logFormat, stdoutW, stderrW, progressBars)
severity_reason: UX/ops nit: not a correctness bug because users can opt in to --log-format=json when piping, but auto-switching matches kubectl/docker/gh conventions and the existing progressBars TTY-gating already establishes the half-pattern.
fix_summary: After the existing TTY detection (L59-60), if logFormat was not explicitly passed (track via a sentinel like '' or a separate flag-changed bool from cobra), default to 'json' when stderrIsTTY=false and 'text' otherwise. Document in the help text. Risk=medium because users with existing pipelines that grep text might see the format flip and complain; cushion with a one-release deprecation.
